first_impression.reaction: My assistant shortlisted it, so she read it and gave me the summary. The first screen is calm and precise. No 'dream wedding' gushing and nothing about being 'affordable', so the brand doesn't lose me straight away. But it's a guide to forms. 'Getting married in Italy as an Australian takes two documents, two countries and a sequence that has to run in the right order.' Useful for whoever runs our paperwork, but it tells me nothing about whether this company can handle a wedding our size, quietly. I read the takeaways and the closing section myself and skimmed the rest.

journey.quote: Most guides online are written for British or American couples and talk about a Certificate of No Impediment, which Italy will not accept from you.
journey.reaction: Good. Precise, and it corrects something other people get wrong. That's the tone I want from anyone touching our legal side.

journey.section: What the Atto Notorio is and where to get it
journey.quote: Get it before you leave, from the Italian consulate for the state where you live.
journey.reaction: We live in Dubai. Every consulate listed is in Australia. Which office covers an Australian who doesn't live in Australia? The page assumes everyone is sitting in Sydney or Melbourne.

journey.section: What the Nulla Osta is and who signs it
journey.quote: Not published: how far ahead Rome and Milan release appointments, and whether a non-Australian partner attends. Your Wedded Advisor confirms both in writing before you book flights.
journey.reaction: I like that they admit what they don't know instead of guessing. Confirming things in writing is how my family office works too.

journey.section: Step by step once you arrive in Italy
journey.quote: Buy a revenue stamp (marca da bollo) at a tobacconist (tabaccaio) first.
journey.reaction: I won't be queuing at a tobacconist the week of my wedding. All of this is written as if the couple does it themselves. I want to read that someone does it for us, and whether the Rome appointment can be handled privately.

journey.quote: A concordat marriage is celebrated by a Catholic priest and takes civil effect once transcribed in the civil register, after publications at the parish and the comune.
journey.reaction: Publications means our names are posted publicly before the wedding. That's exactly how a date leaks. Nobody on this page says whether those notices can be kept discreet, or what that means for privacy.

journey.section: Civil ceremony at the town hall or an approved venue
journey.quote: Not published: which private villas your comune approves for civil ceremonies. Your Wedded Advisor confirms in writing whether your venue qualifies before you sign with it.
journey.reaction: This is the one line that touches what I care about. Can the legal part happen at a property we've taken over completely, not in a public town hall on a piazza? It's raised and then left there.

journey.section: Can Australians legally get married in Italy?
journey.quote: The comune of Bagno a Ripoli, outside Florence, states that foreign citizens may marry there whether they live in Italy or abroad, in a civil, Catholic or other religious ceremony.
journey.reaction: 'Other religious ceremony' is mentioned once and never again. After that it's only civil or Catholic. If our ceremony isn't Catholic, I don't know from this whether it counts legally.

journey.section: Plan the paperwork with one person
journey.quote: A Wedded Advisor works in your time zone, quotes in AUD and stays with you from the first document to the last dance.
journey.reaction: 'From the first document to the last dance' is a bit sweet for my taste, and 'quotes in AUD' tells me they're selling to standard couples. Nothing here says they've done a wedding of 300 guests with outside security.

unanswered_questions: Which office issues the Atto Notorio for an Australian citizen who lives outside Australia, for example in Dubai?
Can the marriage publications at the parish and comune be kept low-profile, and who can see them?
Can the legal civil ceremony be held at an exclusive-use private property rather than a public town hall?
Can the Nulla Osta appointment in Rome or Milan be arranged privately, and can a representative handle the Prefettura and comune steps on our behalf?
Does a non-Catholic religious ceremony have civil effect in Italy, or do we need a separate civil ceremony?
Has Wedded Wonderland delivered weddings of 200 to 400 guests, with private security and VIP transfers?
Is there a private or referral route to enquire, rather than a general form?

turn_offs_found.quote: A Wedded Advisor works in your time zone, quotes in AUD and stays with you from the first document to the last dance.
turn_offs_found.why: Reads like a standard-client pitch. AUD quoting and a catchy line make it feel like a package service, not a private one.

turn_offs_found.quote: Your Wedded Advisor confirms the current requirements with the comune.
turn_offs_found.why: This line, or one just like it, appears roughly ten times. Once is reassuring. By the tenth time it sounds like a template, and it's over-explaining.

would_share_with: My assistant, to keep with the legal checklist for whichever planner we pick
The family office lawyer, for the recognition section

cta_reaction.quote: Speak with a Wedded Advisor about your paperwork timeline, starting with your date and your comune.
cta_reaction.why: I don't make first contact through a website button about paperwork timelines. If someone I trust referred me, or there was a discreet private line, my assistant might call. This invitation is for a couple doing it themselves, not for us.

top_3_changes: Deal with privacy directly: say what the parish and comune publications make public, and whether the legal ceremony can be held at an exclusive-use private property. Where the facts aren't published, list them as questions the planner answers.

Cover Australians who live abroad (Dubai, London): which office issues the Atto Notorio for them. Also say plainly that a representative can handle the Rome or Milan, Prefettura and comune steps, rather than writing as if the couple goes to the tobacconist themselves.

Cut the repeated 'Your Wedded Advisor confirms' lines down to one or two, and make the close quieter: drop 'first document to the last dance' and 'quotes in AUD' and offer a discreet, private way to make contact.
